title: Imonda language
description: Papuan language of Papua New Guinea
extract: Imonda is a Papuan language of Sandaun Province, Papua New Guinea. It has a simple consonant system and a complex vowel system with no phonological tones. Imonda is heavily verb-oriented and does not mark nouns for number or gender but marks number on the verb for subject, object, and several other types of noun phrases. Tense, aspect, negation, and interrogation are also indicated in part on the verb. There is a very high-frequency topic clitic, which can be used on noun phrases, adverbs, or verbs. The language has no coordinating or subordinating conjunctions and fills those roles with other approaches.
